merged.need: A period-over-period delta whose good/bad reading is stated by the caller, not inferred from the arrow's direction
merged.component: StatCard — `deltaDir` conflates direction with sentiment, in the implementation as well as the type
merged.evidence: BRIEF (SCR-M13-01) puts "the overdue total" (M13-16) and the attention list's "payments overdue" and "leads unassigned past 24 hours" (M13-15) on the same dashboard as "won/signed value vs last period, vs target if set" (M13-14). LIVE: StatCard.d.ts documents only `deltaDir?: "up" | "down"`, and StatCard.jsx resolves direction AS sentiment — `const good = deltaDir === "up";` then `background: good ? "var(--success-bg)" : "var(--danger-bg)", color: good ? "var(--success-text)" : "var(--danger-text)"` with a matching arrow path. A rising overdue total renders green with an up arrow and reads as success; overdue falling renders red. On the owner's home screen roughly half the figures are ones where up is bad.

merged.need: A money-amount entry field in the tenant's currency that refuses an out-of-range value and names the honest path, rather than correcting it to a value the person did not type
merged.component: NumberField
merged.evidence: BRIEF (SCR-M11-03, state `Amount-non-positive-refused`): "save is **refused** with the constraint stated in place, no entry is created, and the refusal names the honest path — **a wrong amount is not edited and not typed negative, it is recorded and then reversed**", with the amount "defaulted to the tranche's outstanding, always editable". LIVE: NumberField documents the opposite behaviour — "Commits once on blur or Enter; empty or invalid never commits (the last good value is restored); **a clamped value says so rather than snapping silently**", with `correctionMessage` overriding the generated correction line. Clamp-and-announce is not refuse-and-name-reversal. It also has no currency affordance (`unit` is a trailing string; the only formatter in the system is `inr`/en-IN, display-only, living in the Charts namespace), and its `step`/stepper buttons are the wrong grammar for a payment amount. Input has a `leading` slot but disclaims the job: "onCommit… Always a string — numeric entry with clamping and correction **belongs to NumberField**." The system already knows how to do this correctly one component over — readme.md on TimeField: "A time outside `min`/`max` is **refused with the window named, never clamped**" — so money entry needs the TimeField pattern, not a new idea.

merged.need: An allocation meter against a required total that states the remainder in words and can render an over-allocation
merged.component: ProgressBar — a bare 0–100 `value`
merged.evidence: BRIEF (SCR-M06-09, M06-13, P0): "tranche rows (label + % + ✕) · ＋ Add tranche · **progress bar + validation: 'Total allocation must = 100%'** — post-R12 this is a Generate-time block, shown live as feedback and enforced only at Generate **with the remainder stated ('12% unallocated')**", drawn as `allocation-incomplete-remainder`, with a Data volume requiring "the progress bar and remainder line **always visible at 375 px**". LIVE: ProgressBar has no label, no target, no remainder slot, and no way to render a total above 100% when the rep's rows over-allocate — which is half the failure the live feedback exists to catch. UsageMeter is mechanically closer (denominator, a scale past 100%, a note) and readme.md walls it off: "A billing meter for SCR-M12-04… ProgressBar stays a 6px operation bar with no billing semantics." A proposal's tranche split is not a billing period against a bundle, and borrowing the billing meter is the wrong-instrument failure this audit exists to catch.

merged.need: A held-on-device capture queue that shows how many files are waiting and offers a retry, on the capture surface itself
merged.component: Dropzone — `heldOnDevice?: boolean`
merged.evidence: BRIEF (SCR-M11-03, M11-37, P0): "A photograph captured in the field is held and uploaded when the connection returns, **with its waiting count and a retry shown on the capture screen itself** (F4-21) — but the money entry is a server write." LIVE: Dropzone carries `heldOnDevice?: boolean` documented as "These photos are held on the device and upload once there's a connection. **The one place in the product where anything is kept back**", alongside `state?: "idle"|"uploading"|"error"`, `errorMessage`, per-file `progress` and batch `progress` — and there is no waiting/queued count and no `onRetry` anywhere on the component. The one prop that acknowledges the held queue is a bare boolean, so the two things M11-37 requires the capture screen to show are the two things the capture component cannot show.

merged.need: A stage board whose phone form is one column with a stage filter, not every column stacked
merged.component: Kanban — `stackBelow`
merged.evidence: BRIEF (SCR-M08-01, M08-10, P0): "Desktop shows the full board; **mobile shows one column with a stage filter**", with the named states `mobile-single-column-filter` / `mobile-single-column (stage filter)`. LIVE: Kanban.jsx computes `const stacked = own !== null && own < stackBelow;` then `flexDirection: stacked ? "column" : "row"` over `columns.map(...)` — every one of the nine stage columns renders full width, one after another; at the ruled 200-project volume that is the whole portfolio in one scroll. The prop's own doc sells the wrong answer as the phone form: "Own-width px below which columns **stack vertically** instead of scrolling sideways." The obvious workaround does not close it: a screen could pass a single column with FilterChips above, but Kanban measures its own width with a private ResizeObserver and exposes neither the measurement nor a callback, so the screen cannot know WHEN to switch without duplicating the observer. The component owns the breakpoint and answers it wrongly.

merged.need: A bounded group of labelled chips with an overflow affordance, for a cell or row that holds several at once
merged.component: Chip and Badge are single pills; AvatarGroup is the system's only grouped-token component and it takes people, not labels
merged.evidence: BRIEF (SCR-M01-12, F2-10, P0): "The team list shows **all** roles a person holds as chips", with a Data volume of "each person may carry **several of the twelve preset chips at once** plus a status and a last-active value." BRIEF (SCR-M01-15, M01-34, P0): "every picker and search result badges compliance per those schemes" — several badges per row — and "An empty scheme set means no badges, never an error." LIVE: Chip and Badge are single pills with no grouping, no cap and no overflow; the only grouped-token export is AvatarGroup. DataTable has no per-cell wrap or truncation rule and stacks to one card per record below 640px of its own width, so a cell holding up to twelve role chips has no defined behaviour at either size, and every list screen carrying multi-valued tags decides it again.

merged.need: Authoring one piece of content across several languages, showing per language whether it is authored here or inherited from the primary
merged.evidence: BRIEF (SCR-M07-09, state `language-fallback`): "content is editable per agent language where the owner wants distinct wording; a section answered in one language falls back to the tenant's primary agent language rather than silence — **the design must show which language a section's content actually comes from**"; Data volume: "Eight fixed sections… each holding owner-written content, potentially per agent language (**up to the six agent languages**, M07-15), with fallback to the tenant's primary." LIVE, narrowed honestly: the per-section statement is half-expressible — Textarea has `helper` and could carry "Falling back to Hindi". The switcher half is not: Tabs items are `{value, label}` and SegmentedControl's are `{value, label}` with no badge, count, tone or per-item state, so a six-language switcher cannot show which languages are authored and which are inherited, and the owner cannot see the shape of the work. Accordion's `meta?: string` sits on the SECTION, not on the language.

merged.need: A set of dates the tenant maintains, where each date shows whether the market pack supplied it or the tenant added it, and only the tenant's own can be removed
merged.component: DatePicker — `mode?: "single" | "range"`, `markers` display-only, and a DayMarker whose origin lives in a tooltip
merged.evidence: BRIEF (SCR-M07-06, state `holiday-calendar`): "the market's **pack-supplied** holiday calendar plus **tenant-added** extra holidays"; Numbers carrying provenance: "Holiday dates — pack-supplied market holidays (data from F1-48) plus tenant-added dates"; M07-12 permits "narrower windows and extra holidays only, never wider". LIVE: `mode?: "single" | "range"` — a set of unrelated dates cannot be held, added to or removed at all; `markers?: Record<string, DayMarker>` is display-only and DayMarker is `{tone?: "present"|"absent"|"leave"|"holiday"|"scheduled"|"neutral"; label?: string /** Read out by screen readers and used as the tooltip. */}`. Both origins collapse onto the single `holiday` tone, their only differentiator is the tooltip F8-07 rules out for exactly this kind of provenance, and nothing says which dates the tenant is permitted to delete.

merged.need: A scrubbable period track with transport — play/pause over a continuous or twelve-stop domain — driving a live recompute of the surface beside it, identical in the 2D canvas and the 3D scene
merged.component: AudioPlayer is the only transport in the system and is governed by consent and retention law, not playback; Slider has no playing state and no transport
merged.evidence: BRIEF (SCR-MS-08, M05-45): "irradiance heatmap (legend Poor→Excellent 0/50/100%, **Jan–Dec month scrubber recolouring instantly**, current-month avg access %…)"; (SCR-MS-09, M05-51) "**Play/Pause sun animation; time-of-day 5 AM–7 PM**; sunrise/sunset; sun-position read-out"; (MS6-31) "play/pause animation, time slider, sunrise/sunset readouts, sun-position widget and sun-path arc"; (MS6-36) "month track, optional kWh layer when measured weather exists, and **2D-canvas parity**" — the parity clause is what makes this shared rather than screen-specific. LIVE: SliderProps in full is `value, onInput, onCommit, min, max, step, label, unit, hint, format, steppers, disabled, density, id, style` — no playing state, no play/pause, no per-stop domain, no loop. AudioPlayer is "a call-recording player whose states are governed by consent and retention law, not playback", with `status?: "available"|"consent-declined"|"purged-retention"` — not a simulation clock.

merged.need: A continuous colour-ramp scale with a legend that names its metric and states its floor — for a surface tinted by a value rather than split into named series
merged.component: ChartLegend takes discrete items only; tokens/colors.css has eight categorical chart series and no sequential ramp
merged.evidence: BRIEF (SCR-MS-08, M05-45): "**legend Poor→Excellent 0/50/100%**"; (SCR-MS-09, MS6-36) "geometric-access metric **with its floor stated in the legend**"; (M05-52) "Solar-access view (tints each panel by actual sun)". LIVE: `ChartLegend(props: { items: { label: string; value?: React.ReactNode; color?: string }[] })`, rendered as 8x8 square swatches plus labels — a flat list of discrete stops, with no continuous scale, no min/mid/max and no metric-floor line. tokens/colors.css, read in full this pass, ships "/* Chart palette — ordered, colourblind-safe, sampled from iridescence. Series fills, never text. */ --chart-1…--chart-8" and `--chart-gridline`: eight categorical series and not one sequential ramp, so a designer drawing Poor→Excellent must invent it, which F7-03 forbids.

merged.need: A mode instruction strip: a persistent, politely-announced line stating what the active tool expects and how to cancel it, living for the duration of the mode rather than a timeout
merged.component: Toast / ToastHost — an auto-dismissing notification queue, wrong lifetime and wrong role
merged.evidence: BRIEF (SCR-MS-05, MS2-10): "Draft affordances: crosshair glyph at snapped point, pan disabled while drawing, **live status hint bar (aria-live)**"; (SCR-MS-06, MS3-13) "Placement: pick → **hint bar** → one click drops ONE object at defaults, exits placement, auto-selects; Esc cancels"; (M05-32) "a cancellable touch placement mode **with on-screen instruction**"; (SCR-MS-08, MS6-11) "Measure tool and **per-tool instruction hints**; transient notices with accessible roles; **banner stacking never covers the rails**." LIVE: Toast is "White toast card (16px radius, e5) with a leading semantic icon in a circular tint. **One at a time**", props `tone, title, description, icon, action` — a notification about something that happened, with no role or politeness prop; ToastHost adds `position, max, duration, offset` and "stacks, auto-dismisses, pauses while the pointer is over it". A caller could pass a very large `duration` — the honest escape hatch — and still get a floating card in a dismissal queue rather than an aria-live status BAR bound to a mode's lifetime. Banner, the persistent alternative, is "In-page statement of a fact about what's on screen" whose stacking the brief itself warns must never cover the rails.

verdict: DROPS — 2 capabilities dropped, covering 8 raw rows. (1) 'Per-row provenance inside one DataTable column' (raised as a blocker in block1 twice, block2-5 twice, and as a nit in block7 and block8): REFUTED by its own slice and re-verified by me in the live file. DataTable.jsx ends `export { Tier as ProvenanceTier }` and DataTableColumn carries `render?: (row) => React.ReactNode`, so `render: row => <ProvenanceTier tier={row.tier} withLabel />` places a per-row tier with the shipped API. What survives is not this — it is the primitive's default rendering, which is gap 1. (2) 'AudioPlayer would assert consent/retention facts that do not exist' (block6): REFUTED — AudioPlayer.jsx builds each footnote line conditionally and gates the whole row, so with status defaulted and consentAt/retentionUntil omitted it asserts nothing. What remains is ergonomics, which is a look-and-arrangement matter and not a gap.

NARROWED, not dropped — StatCard. Two slices claimed the tier 'cannot be placed anywhere' on StatCard. StatCard.d.ts types `children?: React.ReactNode`, so a tier CAN be dropped in. The claim is narrowed to what is irreducible and still a blocker: the slot is documented 'e.g. a sparkline node bleeding to card edges', so the adjacency is unspecified and six blocks each pick their own; and StatCard has no `state`, no `onClick` and no band, so freshness, tappable counts and pass/fail verdicts have no expression at all.

DEDUP — roughly 185 raw rows arrived (five slices, each a first pass plus an adversarial refutation, so nearly every finding appeared at least twice). Merged to 46 distinct capabilities. The heaviest merges, which are the ones that change the shape of the problem: the provenance-tier slot was reported 11 times across all five slices under six different names and is now three entries (rendering default, vocabulary, slot); the 44x44 breach was reported from block2-5 and block7 and is one entry naming four sites; DataTable's stacked branch dropping rowActions, isRowMuted and caption arrived from block2-5, block6 and block7 as three findings and is one; the section/block frame arrived from block2-5, block6 and block7 as 'block seams', 'composable home block' and 'titled section card' and is one; StatusChip's closed union arrived from four slices with four different missing vocabularies and is one. A capability reported by five slices is a token- or law-layer problem; a capability reported by one is a surface.

BLOCK 1 VERDICT — NO. The design run cannot start on block 1 today, and blocks 1-6 were NOT clean before this audit. Nine blockers land on block 1's own screens: no application top bar at all (SCR-SHELL-01/02/03, and tokens/spacing.css names --header-h:64px and a --sidebar-w:260px that is not the 72px rail that ships); AppRail's `badge?: boolean` cannot count unread (SCR-SHELL-03); the high-contrast field mode readme.md asserts exists has no implementation in tokens/colors.css, which is a single :root with no second scope (SCR-M01-11); DataTable has no needs-attention row state and no cell commit path for the 400-row inline-fix import (SCR-M01-17); FilterBar.FilterChips is `value?: string`, one-of-N, with no filter-panel body and no range control anywhere in the 54, so M01-38's six dimensions cannot be expressed (SCR-M01-15/16); DocumentPreview is one fixed A4 proposal sheet whose own docstring claims it 'previews all of M01-50 (logo, letterhead, ...)' with no letterhead prop of any kind (SCR-M01-18/19/20); and the three provenance blockers ride every number on every one of those screens. The first block that CAN be drawn is none of them — the provenance, formatting, status-vocabulary and 44px entries are inherited by all 99 screens, so no block is clean until the token- and law-layer entries (gaps 1-11) are closed.

COVERAGE TRACED AND CLEARED — round ten's five fixes were re-opened and each holds for what these briefs need, with two scope limits noted as gaps rather than regressions: Stepper ships the four states including `errors` with `errorCount` ('3 to fix'), plus `rail`/`indicator` and `StepList`, which fully covers M05-03 — its clickability rule is a separate collision with M06-22 and is gap 16, not a re-report. FilterBar's 44px-target-around-a-32-36px-pill law is real and expressed in the component ('Callers get the floor for free and cannot opt out of it') — it is the pattern Kanban, Menu, Banner and SelectionBar should copy and do not. TimeField refuses an out-of-window time with the window named rather than clamping, which is exactly the pattern money entry needs and does not have. BrandColorField measures contrast, answers both directions separately, offers a darkened shade instead of refusing, and renders every verdict as a word plus a glyph — its F7-07 scope statement is gap 7. UsageMeter's denominator, period, tier, 80% tick and past-100% scale all hold for a sold bundle; the no-rate case and the missing loading/error states are gap 13.

ALSO CLEARED against the live files, so the holes are legible against real coverage: DataTable's sorting, pagination, selection band, own-width stacking, loading/empty/error and exported ProvenanceTier; Image/ImageFrame/Thumbnail's three-state footprint fixed before the fetch, plus `referenceOnly` and `staleAt` (which covers SCR-F5-05's captures-fallback and is the precedent numbers lack); AudioPlayer's consent-declined and purged-retention as separate non-error states; ChartFrame's `provenance` marked 'Required on anything user-facing' and its four states; MapSurface's four honest states including tiles-unavailable, its overlay slot and 44px controls; NoConnection as the one full-screen state rather than a per-surface one; CoachMark, Toast/ToastHost, Modal, Dropzone's upload states, Checkbox/Radio/Switch, SearchField, OtpInput, QRCode, Breadcrumb, Avatar/AvatarGroup, Wordmark/LogoTile; Kanban's always-visible move buttons as the keyboard-and-touch answer to HTML5 drag (right intent, wrong target size); Calendar/DatePicker markers; and the contrast floor itself, which is measured, tokenised and genuinely enforceable — tokens/colors.css carries white/canvas/own-tint ratios per token and the marks-vs-words split is real.
